# NEXORA · Master source 2.0

Learn. Explore. Innovate.

This is the editable continuation of the existing NEXORA application. It includes a browser frontend, a Node HTTP backend, Supabase SQL migration, server-side OpenAI integration, curriculum, SVG teaching models, and automated tests. The palette is navy, blue, amber, and neutral paper. No purple or green brand colors are used.

## Install and run

Requirements: Node.js **22.9 or newer**, npm, and a modern browser. Python 3 is needed only to rebuild the ZIP. There are no third-party runtime dependencies.

```sh
npm ci
cp .env.example .env
npm start
```

On Windows, use `copy .env.example .env`. Open **http://127.0.0.1:3000**. Guest lessons, projects, progress, models, and the code playground work without external credentials. Account and AI requests return explicit configuration errors until their services are configured. The application never supplies fake accounts or canned AI fallback answers.

```sh
npm test
npm run build
node --env-file-if-exists=.env build/server/index.js
```

Stop the development server first if it uses the same port. `npm run build` syntax-checks all browser/server modules and creates `build/dist` and `build/server`; it does not require a bundler. `dist/` contains the editable frontend source, despite the directory name. `build/` is generated output and is excluded from the source archive.

## Curriculum and age experiences

Each subject has six topic paths. Each path includes prerequisites, a concept explanation, two worked examples, a manipulable model with captions, a real-world investigation, misconceptions, three assessed checks with feedback, a project notebook, and a rubric. Passing the guided check records the Understand lesson; passing all three records Apply and unlocks the next topic. The original standalone foundations remain available and existing progress is preserved.

| Subject | Six topics |
| --- | --- |
| Mathematics | Numbers and place value; fractions; algebra; geometry; functions; probability |
| Science | Matter; forces; energy; living systems; electricity; Earth and space |
| Coding & Programming | Algorithms; variables; conditions; loops; functions; data structures and search |
| Computer Science & Technology | Binary; memory; networks; databases; security and permissions; AI evaluation |
| Engineering & Robotics | Design; mechanisms; circuits; sensors and actuators; feedback; automation |
| Logical Reasoning & Data | Patterns; deduction; flowcharts; data visualization; sampling; optimization |

**Under 10 — Story World:** model-first teaching, short stories, objects and visual transformations, large choices, short guided checks, 36 concrete making activities, and read-aloud controls. The primary questions and projects use simpler tasks than the older pathways.

**Ages 10–12 — Discovery Lab:** mission navigation, notebook layout, variable manipulation, predictions compared with computed outcomes, and investigation prompts.

**Ages 13–14 — Challenge Studio:** structured study, technical diagrams, multi-step practice, reasoning notes, and editable JavaScript investigations.

**Ages 15–20+ — Research Workspace:** compact professional workspace, theory extensions, assumptions, parameter sweep tables, downloadable computed CSV data, project evidence, and mastery estimates.

There are **144 topic/age journeys** (36 topics × 4 experiences), plus **24 existing foundation treatments**. The factual topic core is shared for older learners; interaction, scaffolding, visual presentation, and advanced extensions differ. This is a bounded authored STEM curriculum, not exhaustive coverage of every school or university syllabus. The assessments are small numeric checks, not accredited exams. Project reflections are stored and self-assessed against rubrics; they are not automatically graded. Subject experts should review educational depth, model assumptions, and suitability before institutional use.

## Progress, accessibility, and learning tools

Guest progress uses `nexora-v1` in localStorage. Existing version-1 data is normalized without deleting valid completions, notes, or preferences. Account caches use separate learner IDs. Completion records are unioned during synchronization conflicts; XP is recomputed and never awarded twice for a completed lesson. Unassisted completion earns 50 XP, assisted completion 30. First discovery and six-subject milestones derive from completion records. Backups export/import as JSON.

Topics unlock sequentially within each subject and age experience. Continue Learning restores the last topic. Attempt accuracy and hint use drive guided/independent/extension recommendations; this is a simple evidence rule, not a psychometrically calibrated adaptive algorithm. The initial placement question covers mathematics only. Mastery estimates use the current age experience, and the progress page shows completed topic counts.

Read aloud uses browser speech synthesis with speed, pause/resume, and stop controls. Voices and actual audible output depend on the device. All concepts remain available as text/captions. No audio autoplays. System reduced-motion and the still-frame preference are respected; Play becomes a manual model step in reduced-motion mode.

Focus mode hides distracting application panels, has a configurable 5–90 minute study timer, pause/resume, a configurable break reminder, and the last 100 completed sessions. It does not block websites, other apps, notifications, or leaving the tab; browser timer throttling can delay reminders. It does not enforce a break or run a separate break countdown.

The JavaScript playground runs small synchronous examples in a one-second Web Worker with a 100-line output cap. It does not install packages, execute server code, or provide a general-purpose IDE. Do not use it to run untrusted third-party programs; worker time limits are not a hardened multi-tenant execution service.

## Supabase accounts and database

Follow **[database/README.md](database/README.md)** for the migration, RLS details, and exact confirmation/recovery email templates. Set these server-only environment variables:

```dotenv
SUPABASE_URL=https://YOUR-PROJECT.supabase.co
SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=YOUR_LEGACY_ANON_KEY
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=YOUR_LEGACY_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
```

Never put these values in `dist/`, a public build variable, source control, or the ZIP. This implementation uses the legacy JWT API keys. Supabase Auth stores and hashes passwords; NEXORA does not store plaintext passwords. Registration collects name, unique username, email, password, and confirmation. Login accepts email or username. Email confirmation, password recovery, profile name editing, initials avatar, logout, refresh sessions, and per-account progress are implemented. Cloud status changes only after actual requests succeed.

The backend keeps session tokens in HttpOnly cookies scoped to `/api`, with SameSite=Lax and Secure in production. Progress/profile requests use the learner JWT under RLS. Only the server uses the service-role key for username lookup. Separate guest work can be explicitly imported from Profile Settings; it is not silently mixed into an account.

Live Supabase registration, email delivery, database migration execution, cross-device synchronization, and RLS isolation have **not been verified in this environment**, because no Supabase credentials are configured. Automated tests cover transport contracts, errors, UI, and isolation using clearly marked fixtures. Follow the live verification checklist in the database guide before enabling accounts for real learners. MFA, account deletion UI, email changes, and avatar uploads are not implemented.

## Real AI tutor setup

Set `OPENAI_API_KEY` only in the Node server environment. Optional `OPENAI_MODEL` defaults to `gpt-4.1-mini`; choose a Responses-API-compatible model available to your provider account. API access and billing are required.

The assistant supports lesson-context explanations, graduated hints, step-by-step help, code debugging, summaries, practice generation, and follow-up questions. It receives canonical curriculum content from the server and age-specific teaching instructions. Client-supplied arbitrary lesson text is not trusted. Loading, cancellation, retry, missing configuration, rate limit, timeout, and provider errors are handled explicitly. Provider responses are displayed as text, not executable HTML.

The server uses `https://api.openai.com/v1/responses`, requests `store:false`, and caps conversation/history/body/output sizes. It limits concurrent requests to 3, requests per client IP to 10/minute, and successful requests per process to `AI_DAILY_REQUEST_LIMIT` (default 100) per day. `AI_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` defaults to 800, capped at 1500. The upstream timeout is 25 seconds. Limits reset on process restart; use durable per-user limits and provider spending caps for a public deployment.

The active conversation sends age band, selected lesson identifiers, a coarse mastery estimate, and up to 12 messages. It does not send the full learner account, notes, or full progress history. Chats are kept in the active tab and cleared when context/account changes. Provider retention is governed by its terms. The assistant cannot execute code, browse, grade projects, or change progress. Live model output and teaching quality have **not been tested without an API credential**. Fixtures exist only in tests and are never substituted for real answers in the application.

## Deployment

Deploy the complete Node application to a Node-capable HTTPS host, with the browser and `/api/*` on the same origin. Use `npm ci && npm run build` as the build command and `node build/server/index.js` as the production start command when the host injects environment variables. Set `HOST=0.0.0.0`, the host-assigned `PORT`, `NODE_ENV=production`, and `COOKIE_SECURE=true`. Keep the reverse proxy Host/Origin consistent with the browser origin. Set Supabase Site URL to that origin and configure SMTP and both email templates. Allow server egress to your Supabase host and api.openai.com. No local database volume is needed; account data lives in Supabase.

The existing owner-private **Sites publication serves static assets**. It supports guest learning and distributing the ZIP, but it does not execute this Node backend. AI and accounts honestly report unavailable there. Setting secrets on static-only hosting does not create API routes. To activate these services, deploy the included Node backend as described above. `.openai/hosting.json` preserves the existing private Site identity; it is not required by the Node runtime.

Security headers are applied by the Node server; `_headers` is included for compatible static hosts. Production operators should configure HTTPS, monitoring, backups, provider spending limits, and durable abuse controls appropriate to their deployment. Local learner caches are not encrypted storage. XP/progress are learner-managed records, not tamper-proof certification or a competitive leaderboard.

## Testing and archive reproduction

```sh
npm test
npm run build
```

Tests cover curriculum fields and all 144 topic combinations, calculated model relationships, progression gates, idempotent XP, progress normalization/merging, account validation, username conflicts, session handling, recovery, and tutor transport/error handling. This JavaScript project has no TypeScript compiler or lint command; build syntax checks are not presented as a type-check or lint result.

For browser tests, install Playwright separately (`npm install --no-save --package-lock=false playwright` and `npx playwright install chromium`), start `npm start`, and run:

```sh
node tests/navigation-browser.cjs
node tests/auth-browser.cjs
node tests/recovery-browser.cjs
node tests/tutor-browser.cjs
node tests/browser-test.cjs
node tests/course-browser.cjs
node tests/course-tools-browser.cjs
```

Use `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` for a preinstalled module and `CHROMIUM_PATH` for an existing Chromium executable. Tests use disposable local learner data and explicitly mocked external-service fixtures. They do not contact live providers. Evidence is in `verification/`; screenshots and temporary logs go to ignored `work/`.

```sh
python3 scripts/package.py
python3 -m zipfile -t dist/NEXORA-MASTER-SOURCE.zip
```

The source ZIP uses an explicit source-directory allowlist. It excludes real `.env` files, Git metadata, node_modules, generated build output, temporary work, caches, private learner data, and nested ZIPs. It includes the lockfile and configuration example. See **COMPLETION.md** for the tests actually run and remaining limitations.
